from openpyxl import load_workbook
from pathlib import Path

# Paths
spreadsheet_path = "/mnt/data/spreadsheet/94-8/1_94-8_input.xlsx"
output_path = "/mnt/data/outputs/94-8_0_2d47d601/1_94-8_output.xlsx"

# Load workbook and target sheet
wb = load_workbook(spreadsheet_path)
ws = wb["BeforeVBA"]

# Hard-coded valid Item/Sku pairs.
# To adapt this to 100+ items, add more ("Item", "Sku") tuples to this set.
valid_pairs = {
    ("RPC0094", "17343D"),
    ("RPC0097", "17263D"),
    ("RPC0068", "17232B"),
}

# Work only in the data area of columns A:F below the header.
min_row = 2
max_row = ws.max_row
min_col = 1
max_col = 6

# Read the current rows in A:F and keep only matching Item/Sku pairs
kept_rows = []
for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=min_row, max_row=max_row, min_col=min_col, max_col=max_col, values_only=True):
    item = "" if row[3] is None else str(row[3]).strip()
    sku = "" if row[4] is None else str(row[4]).strip()
    if (item, sku) in valid_pairs:
        kept_rows.append(row)

# Clear only the allowed data cells in A:F, then write the kept records compacted upward
for r in range(min_row, max_row + 1):
    for c in range(min_col, max_col + 1):
        ws.cell(row=r, column=c).value = None

for offset, row_values in enumerate(kept_rows):
    r = min_row + offset
    if r > max_row:
        break
    for c, value in enumerate(row_values, start=min_col):
        ws.cell(row=r, column=c).value = value

# Save to the required output path
Path(output_path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
wb.save(output_path)
